title: Sheaf cotangent stalks, section maps and ring localization
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space and $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}=s(\Omega^1_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B)$, using the standard resolution in sheaves: $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on, with faces and degeneracies from free-algebra evaluation and unit. Here the free sheaf algebra is the sheafification of the sectionwise polynomial algebra, $s$ takes alternating faces in nonpositive cohomological degrees, and sheaf differentials are sheafifications of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For every open $V\subseteq T$, the canonical section maps $L_{\mathcal B(V)/\mathcal A(V)}\to L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}(V)$ commute with restriction, and their sheafification gives the displayed sheaf complex. For every continuous map $u:T\prime\to T$, inverse image gives a canonical identification $u^{-1}L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\simeq L_{u^{-1}\mathcal B/u^{-1}\mathcal A}$, natural in the map of sheaves of rings; these identifications are compatible with composition of continuous maps. For every $t\in T$ there is a canonical identification $(L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A})_t\simeq L_{\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t}$, natural in maps of sheaves of rings and open restrictions. For a homomorphism of commutative rings $A\to B$ and multiplicative subsets $S\subseteq A$, $W\subseteq B$ such that $S$ maps into $W$, the canonical map $L_{B/A}\otimes_B W^{-1}B\to L_{W^{-1}B/S^{-1}A}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, compatible with successive localizations. Ring cotangent complexes use the standard construction of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence].

proof.text: Sheafification $a$ is a geometric inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-standard-differential-comparison] to $a$ from the presheaf topos. On that topos the standard construction is sectionwise, so its alternating complex evaluates to $L_{\mathcal B(V)/\mathcal A(V)}$. The comparison identifies its sheafification with the displayed sheaf complex, including faces and degeneracies. The sheafification unit, evaluated on each open $V$, gives the actual section map into $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}(V)$; On differential tensors it sends $\mathrm dp\otimes b$ to $\mathrm d(\eta p)\otimes\eta b$, where $\eta$ is the sheafification unit; unit naturality for inclusions of opens proves restriction compatibility.

For continuous $u:T'\to T$, the inverse-open functor preserves finite limits and covers. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] it gives the geometric inverse image $u^{-1}$, additive and exact on abelian sheaves. It therefore preserves kernels, images and their quotients, hence cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms, also with the transported module actions. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-standard-differential-comparison]: its actual complex isomorphism descends to the required derived identification. Its ring-square naturality and identity/composition clauses give precisely the asserted coherence.

Apply step 2 to the inclusion $i:\{t\}\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk], evaluation on the singleton is the stalk, and the unit sends sections to their germs. A sheaf on a singleton is determined by this value, with terminal value on the empty open. Thus the comparison is $(L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A})_t\cong L_{\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t}$; its module action is the stalk action since $(bm)_t=b_t m_t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], stalks preserve kernels and cokernels, hence cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms, so this comparison descends to derived categories. Ring-map naturality comes from step 2; restriction to a neighbourhood leaves these germs unchanged.

Put $D=S^{-1}A$, $C=W^{-1}B$. The fraction formula $a/s\mapsto f(a)/f(s)$ gives $D\to C$, since $f(S)\subseteq W$. By [lem-trf-localization-cotangent-vanishing], $L_{D/A}=L_{C/B}=0$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], $C$ is flat over $B$. Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-zero-relative-square]. Its two canonical arrows are $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/D}$, whose composite is the square comparison. Its flat chain representative is precisely the canonical map in the statement and is a quasi-isomorphism. For successive localizations, apply its composition clauses to the induced successive ring squares: both ordinary and derived composites agree with the direct comparison under the specified tensor associator.
